Bekk. Anecd. p. 346, 9 'Αδριαναὶ γυναῖκες [Adrian women]. The verse is an Ionic tetrameter, in which Hermann conjectured that Aeschylus preferred the Ionic form 'Adpinναί [Adrian women] as more poetic, just as Euripides said τᾶς Ἀδριηνᾶς [of the Adriatic woman] Hipp. 735. On the manner of mourning which the women by the Po are to observe, see Polybius 2, 16, Scymnus v. 399, Diodorus 5, 23.
And Adrian women will have a manner of wailing.
